title: Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst
summary: The frontline defender who monitors, detects, analyzes, and responds to real-time security alerts and anomalies across enterprise networks and endpoints.
dailyResponsibilities: Triage and investigate incoming SIEM alerts generated by EDR, firewall, and identity systems
Perform packet analysis and host artifact inspection to differentiate true security incidents from false positives
Contain compromised endpoints by isolating hosts on the network and revoking compromised credentials
Draft incident response documentation, IOC lists, and post-mortem analysis summaries
keySkills: SIEM navigation and query authoring (Splunk, Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel)
Log analysis across Windows Event Logs, Linux syslog, and web server access logs
Understanding common attack techniques mapped to MITRE ATT&CK framework
Network packet analysis using Wireshark and tcpdump
progression: Tier 1 SOC Analyst (Alert triage & initial scoping)
Tier 2 Incident Handler (Deep forensic analysis & containment)
Tier 3 Threat Hunter / Detection Engineer (Proactive adversary discovery)
SOC Lead / Security Operations Manager

title: Penetration Tester / Ethical Hacker
summary: Authorized security specialist hired to legally simulate real-world cyberattacks against systems, applications, and networks to uncover security weaknesses before adversaries do.
dailyResponsibilities: Conduct in-scope vulnerability assessments and manual exploitation against client networks
Test web, mobile, and API interfaces for business logic flaws and OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities
Execute Active Directory attacks, credential dumping, and privilege escalation techniques
Write formal executive and technical penetration testing reports detailing reproduction steps and remediation
keySkills: Network enumeration and service fingerprinting with Nmap
Web application interception and manual testing using Burp Suite Professional
Linux and Windows internal privilege escalation vectors
Clear technical report writing with actionable developer recommendations
recommendedPaths: Path C — Ethical Hacking & Practical Pentesting
progression: Junior Penetration Tester (Assisted network & web testing)
Senior Penetration Tester (Full-scope client assessments & red teaming)
Principal Red Teamer / Offensive Operations Lead
VP of Security Assessment / Founder

title: Application Security (AppSec) Engineer
summary: Bridges the gap between software development and cybersecurity by securing source code, building secure CI/CD pipelines, and conducting security architecture reviews.
dailyResponsibilities: Integrate SAST, DAST, SCA, and secret scanning into GitHub Actions and GitLab CI pipelines
Perform manual code audits to identify security defects in Python, TypeScript, Java, and Go
Work alongside product development teams to design secure authentication, authorization, and cryptographic workflows
Manage vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty triage pipelines
keySkills: Deep understanding of web protocols, browser security models, and OWASP Top 10
Proficiency in modern programming languages (TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go)
Threat modeling methodologies (STRIDE, PASTA)
Secure API design, JWT/OAuth validation, and session management
progression: Junior AppSec Engineer (Pipeline scanning & vulnerability triage)
Senior AppSec Engineer (Architecture review, threat modeling, custom tooling)
Staff Security Engineer / Product Security Architect
Chief Product Security Officer (CPSO)

title: Cloud Security Engineer
summary: Specializes in designing, implementing, and maintaining secure cloud architectures, multi-tenant guardrails, and automated compliance policies across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
dailyResponsibilities: Implement zero-trust Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies following least-privilege principles
Deploy Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation) with integrated policy-as-code guardrails (Open Policy Agent)
Monitor cloud environments for configuration drift, open storage buckets, and compromised cloud keys
Coordinate automated remediation scripts for non-compliant cloud workloads
keySkills: Cloud architecture and IAM policy structure across major providers (AWS/Azure/GCP)
Container security, Kubernetes RBAC, and container image scanning
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and CI/CD security controls
Cloud security posture management (CSPM) and Cloud Workload Protection (CWPP)
entryCertifications: Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500)
progression: Cloud Systems / DevOps Engineer
Cloud Security Engineer (Policy design & monitoring)
Principal Cloud Security Architect (Zero-trust enterprise architecture)
Head of Enterprise Infrastructure Security

title: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Analyst
summary: Evaluates enterprise business risks, ensures strict regulatory compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR), and formulates security policies for the entire organization.
dailyResponsibilities: Coordinate internal and external audit readiness assessments for certifications such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001
Assess third-party vendor risks by reviewing security questionnaires and SOC 2 Type II reports
Maintain the enterprise risk register, scoring vulnerabilities based on business impact and likelihood
Draft, update, and communicate company-wide security policies, acceptable use guidelines, and incident response plans
keySkills: Regulatory frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS Controls, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR)
Vendor risk management and third-party security evaluation
Effective cross-functional communication between engineering, legal, and executive teams
Quantitative and qualitative risk assessment modeling
progression: GRC Specialist / IT Compliance Associate
Senior Risk Analyst / Compliance Manager
Director of Information Security Governance & Risk
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

title: Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) Analyst
summary: Investigates sophisticated cyber breaches, recovers forensic evidence from infected systems, reverse-engineers malware, and determines root cause.
dailyResponsibilities: Perform forensically sound disk imaging, RAM memory acquisition, and artifact preservation
Analyze master file tables (MFT), registry hives, event logs, and shimcache to build intrusion timelines
Analyze malware binaries in sandbox environments to extract command-and-control indicators (IOCs)
Testify or produce legal-grade evidentiary reports regarding cyber incident scope and data exfiltration
keySkills: Forensic artifact analysis (Windows Registry, Prefetch, Amcache, LNK files, Shellbags)
Memory forensics using Volatility 3 to uncover injected code and hidden processes
Timeline analysis with tools such as Plaso/log2timeline and EZ Tools
Understanding chain of custody, legal evidence handling, and anti-forensic countermeasures
progression: DFIR Incident Responder (Host analysis & evidence collection)
Senior Forensic Investigator (Complex root-cause & APT attribution)
Incident Response Engagement Lead / Threat Intel Lead
Director of Incident Response & Forensic Services
